STEP 1 - scope screening of the five proposals against the frozen bundles.
Read: all five bundles (d69fbb2eeb4c9ab0, 6b5ae2abeecaab25, df96b282930cef5f, bc49cd02b60c2754, 73aab3babfa88c58) plus the shared ledger E18-E25 and the train-only probes E5/E6.
Observed: every proposal keeps the baseline balanced Sinkhorn and takes the hard level index as row-argmax of the balanced plan (cohrank "k_i = argmax_k P_ik"; CURV_COH "row argmax of P as in the baseline code"; curvature-stratum "baseline's argmax over the balanced plan"; hyperbolic_behavior "argmax_k P_ik from this balanced P"; scc-l1 "code(i)=argmax_k P1_ik"). None replaces the balanced assignment with a plain argmin, so the anti-collapse clause is respected by all five and none is OUT_OF_SCOPE on that ground.
Also observed: all five bundles contain the same generic proxy results - E11 geometry_operator_valid PASS, E12 behavior_dependency FAIL, E13 geometry_dependency PASS (1 of top-1 changed), E14 CANDIDATE_PATH_NOT_RUN, E10 only "proposed" Euclidean control - so the bundles do not differentiate the candidates; only the proposal text, the shared probes (E5 graph, E6 prefix statistic) and the shared ledger (E18-E25) can.
Discriminators I will use: (a) faithfulness to the baseline's Sinkhorn marginals/temperature/iterations and to the baseline objective, (b) whether the coupling constant is derived or defaulted, (c) magnitude of the perturbation of the level-1 plan, (d) whether the behaviour partner coordinate is a code radius (the ledger's weakest family) or an in-rho learned stratum, (e) per-step cost.
Open: final ordering and reasons.

STEP 2 - evidence-grounded comparison and ranking decision.
Shared evidence used: E5 measured train graph 118315 edges, mean_outgoing_degree 5.4526 -> sparse, so item-level triangle cohesion is noisy; E6 same_first_prefix_rate 0.0907 vs permuted null 0.067 -> the level-1 prefix carries only a weak behavioural signal, so heavy forcing of behaviour homogeneity at level 1 is risky. Ledger E18-E25 (all comparable_to_frozen=false, global_batch 16384, none at the frozen protocol): best observed 0.05459705 (BRANCH_CONDITIONED_FRECHET_RESIDUAL, E19), 0.05438813 (CURV-RESID-CONTRAST, E24), 0.05165480 (CONCMID-GEO-SID, E22), 0.05000087 (COOC_RANK_FRECHET, E23), 0.04822507 (BEHDIR-L4, E18), and the radius-parameter arm BRad-RQ lowest at 0.04460384 and 0.03060638 (E20/E21). Nothing in the ledger reaches the 0.065 target, so ranking is comparative plausibility.
Decision: (1) CURV_COH_PREFIX_SINKHORN - only candidate whose behaviour offset is capped at 10% of the measured curved-distance scale and confined to level 1, so Sinkhorn and Euclidean levels 2-3 stay verbatim (smallest perturbation of the balanced plan; penalty noted: its a_k is code depth, the BRad-RQ radius family). (2) curvature-stratum-sinkhorn-v1 - cleanest modification (cost matrix only, no second loss), derived beta from the epoch-0 median distance, stratum in rho space not radius, but the tent kernel at median-distance scale risks a hard behaviour-quantile partition on a sparse graph (E5) and can cost the coherence that BEHDIR-L4 (0.0482) lost. (3) cohrank-curvature-sinkhorn-v1 - well specified, derived scales, but median-scale offset at all three levels plus a full-weight curvature-variance loss, ~785k curved entries/step. (4) scc-l1-curvcoherence - renormalises the cost by the batch median (changes effective entropy), behaviour centres from detached running-mean buffers fed by a discarded first Sinkhorn pass. (5) hyperbolic_behavior_curvature_sinkhorn_v1 - couples to a centred code radius with arbitrary sign (the BRad-RQ family), D_med renormalisation plus a 16k-edge contrastive term, lambda=1 default.
Open: none; full answer appended next.

STEP 3 - final answer (complete, stands alone).

the gentlest perturbation of the balanced plan, which matters because E6 shows the level-1 prefix carries only 0.0907 same-prefix rate against a 0.067 null and the shared ledger tops out at 0.05460 (E19 BRANCH_CONDITIONED_FRECHET_RESIDUAL) with the behaviour-heavy radius arm at 0.04460/0.03061 (E20/E21) - its one handicap, a_k being code depth, is exactly that radius family."}, {"idea_id": "curvature-stratum-sinkhorn-v1", "position": 2, "reason": "RANK: curvature-stratum-sinkhorn-v1 | position=2 | reason=changes only the level-1 cost matrix (no second loss, no extra pathway) and keeps the baseline Sinkhorn/STE/codebooks and Euclidean levels 2-3 untouched, with beta derived from the epoch-0 median distance and strata initialised at rank quantiles logit((k+0.5)/K), i.e. a learned stratum in rho space rather than the code-radius coordinate that sits at the bottom of the ledger (E20/E21 BRad-RQ 0.04460/0.03061); E18 0.04823) warn is expensive."}, {"idea_id": "scc-l1-curvcoherence", "position": 4, "reason": "RANK: scc-l1-curvcoherence | position=4 | reason=renormalises the level-1 cost by the batch median d_c, which changes the effective entropy strength of the baseline Sinkhorn (conceded in its own risk list) and departs from the E8 'baseline Sinkhorn verbatim' property; its behaviour centres b_k come from detached running-mean buffers fed by a first Sinkhorn pass whose plan is then discarded, so the joint behaviour-geometry dependency is the hardest of the five to attribute in a single run (E14 shows no bundle has an executed joint-path check), and the added L_curv is weighted at the commitment beta."}, {"idea_id": "hyperbolic_behavior_curvature_sinkhorn_v1", "position": 5, "reason": "RANK: hyperbolic_behavior_curvature_sinkhorn_v1 | position=5 | reason=couples behaviour rank to the centred code radius rhat_k, a coordinate whose sign is arbitrary by construction (its own risk) and the family the ledger puts lowest (E20/E21 BRad-RQ 0.04460/0.03061); it additionally divides d_c by a batch median D_med (temperature scale relative to the baseline), adds a graph-edge contrastive term over up to 16k edges on top of the cost offset, and uses lambda=1.0 as a documented default rather than a

measured quantity, so three simultaneous changes make the single frozen run least interpretable (E12/E14 leave the joint dependency unverified in every bundle)."}], "objection": "No bundle contains an executed joint-path dependency check: E12 behavior_dependency is FAIL and E14 CANDIDATE_PATH_NOT_RUN in all five bundles, and E10 is only 'proposed', so every ranking above rests on the generic proxies plus shared evidence, not on a demonstrated coupling. The shared ledger cannot support the 0.065 target: every arm is comparable_to_frozen=false (global_batch 16384) and the best is 0.05460 (E19), 0.05439 (E24), 0.05165 (E22), 0.05000 (E23), 0.04823 (E18), 0.04460 and 0.03061 (E20/E21), so no behaviour-hyperbolic coupling in the record has yet produced the required lift. Finally the behavioural antecedent is thin for all five: E5 measures 118315 edges at mean_outgoing_degree 5.4526 (a sparse graph where triangle cohesion is near-zero for most items) and E6 measures same-first-prefix 0.0907 against a 0.067 permuted null, i.e. the level-1 prefix that all five proposals want to stratify by curvature currently carries only a weak behavioural signal - the first place to look if the winning candidate lands at or below baseline."}
